data.description:
# Gate leak: completed/in_review items with no audit (flag + doctor report)

## Problem statement

Work items can reach `completed`/`in_review` — and ship — with **no audit record at all**, and the no-audit population is invisible: 12 of 52 `completed`/`in_review` items had no audit, including the root-level `WL-0MU9Z7L8X00117BI` (Client retry does not honour Retry-After), advanced to `completed`/`in_review` and shipped (`5ccc2ae3`) without one. `closeDescendants` (`src/commands/close.ts`) closes every descendant via `closeSingle` without requiring a child audit, and nothing prevents a `status: completed` + `stage: in_review` transition without an audit. The gap must be made **visible** (report) and **guarded** (flag at closure/advance), with an explicit, recorded escape hatch (waiver).

## Users and user stories

- **Producer reviewing the release queue** — As a producer, I want `wl doctor` to list every `completed`/`in_review` item with no audit (with parent/child relationship and age), so the gap cannot silently accumulate and I can decide to audit or waive each one.
- **Release/automation operator** — As an operator, I want closing an unaudited root item to emit a clear, non-fatal warning, so I notice the gap at closure time without breaking existing automation or forcing `--force` for every legacy item.
- **Agent implementing/reviewing a sub-tree** — As an agent, I want a child closed under a fresh-audited parent to be treated as *covered* (derived, per the P6 child-coverage decision) and **not** flagged, so the report reflects reality and does not re-open already-covered work.
- **Developer handling a legitimate exception** — As a developer, I want to record an explicit waiver with a reason, so a deliberate audit exception is auditable rather than silent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Explicit, durable waiver mechanism.** A `wl` command records an explicit waiver on a work item (recommended surface: `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<text>" [--author <name>]` and `wl audit-unwaive <id>`), stored durably and machine-readable and surfaced in `wl show --json`. Verification: a test proves waive creates the record and unwaive removes it; the record is round-tripped through sync/JSONL.
2. **Closure/advance guard flags `completed`/`in_review` without a fresh audit (flag, not hard block).** When the non-force close/advance path closes a **root** item whose audit is absent or stale per the shared `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint, currentFingerprint)` predicate, and no waiver is recorded, the CLI emits a clear non-fatal warning naming the gap. `wl close --force` remains the explicit escape hatch (bypasses and records the bypass as a waiver/reason). Verification: closing an unaudited root item emits the warning; closing a root with a fresh audit or a waiver does not.
3. **Child coverage is honoured (derived, per `WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L`).** In both the close path and the report, a child (`parentId` set) is *covered* iff its **direct** parent has a fresh audit (reuse `isCoveredByParent`/`isAuditFresh` from `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) — a covered child is not flagged; a child with no fresh parent audit is flagged unless waived. Coverage stays **derived at read time; nothing is persisted** (no schema migration for coverage). Verification: test — child under a fresh-audited parent is not flagged; child under a stale/unaudited parent is flagged; waived child is not flagged.
4. **`wl doctor` report of the no-audit population.** A read-only report (recommended: `wl doctor audit-gaps [--json]`, no `--apply`) lists every `completed`/`in_review` item with **no audit record**, showing for each: root vs `child of <parent-id>`, age (derived from `updatedAt`/`activityAt`), and coverage/waiver status (covered / uncovered / waived). Verification: a CLI/integration test against a fixture DB asserts the reported rows and fields, and that covered/waived items are excluded from the flagged set (or shown as covered/waived).
5. **Tests and documentation.** Tests cover all three required scenarios from the description — root item advanced without audit is flagged; child under an audited parent is not flagged; a waiver suppresses the flag — plus report field content. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README`, CLI help text, and any relevant docs-site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, do not fork, the freshness predicate.** `isAuditFresh` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` is the single source of truth for "fresh audit" (WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE, WL-0MUBVH7ZR009PP80, WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K). The guard/report must call it — no competing `auditedAt`-vs-`updatedAt` comparison.
- **Non-fatal guard.** The closure guard must not break existing automation; it warns/flags. A hard block was explicitly avoided (see Assumptions).
- **Derived coverage, no coverage persistence.** Per WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L, child coverage is derived at read time; do not add a persisted coverage reference or coverage-specific migration.
- **Migrations are review-gated.** Any new column (only the waiver record, if a DB-backed design is chosen) must go through `src/migrations/` and `wl doctor upgrade`, never a silent ALTER.
- **CLI and herdr agree.** Where the no-audit/covered notion is consumed by both the CLI and the herdr display/dispatch paths, keep the predicate in `@worklog/shared` (single source of truth).
- **Scope discipline.** This item owns *reporting and flagging* the gate leak; it must not re-open the P6 display work or the root-only dispatch decision (WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC).

## Existing state

- `src/commands/close.ts` — `closeSingle()` sets `status: completed` / `stage: done` with no audit check; `closeDescendants()` closes the whole subtree via `closeSingle()`. The recursive path only requires the **parent** to be `in_review` with `auditResult.readyToClose === true`; `--force` bypasses all checks.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — `doctor stage-sync` already detects stale status/stage combinations (with `--apply`), but has no audit rule/report. `doctor` also has `prune`, `foreign-items`, `priority`, `file-paths`, `migrate`.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint?, currentFingerprint?)` (content-fingerprint primary, legacy 60 s time floor fallback) and `isCoveredByParent(item, parentAudit)` (derived depth-1 child coverage) already exist.
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — `audit_results` table (latest-only, sole source of truth for audit state); `workitems` has no waiver/coverage column. `src/migrations/index.ts` has the fingerprint migration precedent.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` documents derived child coverage and root-only audit dispatch.
- No `waiver` concept exists anywhere in `src/`, `packages/`, or `docs/`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce an **explicit, durable waiver** for the no-audit gate (recommended: `wl audit-waive` / `wl audit-unwaive`, backed by a nullable waiver record) — the only permitted schema addition in this item.
2. Add a shared **audit-gap predicate** that classifies an item as `covered` (child under fresh-audited direct parent), `waived`, or `uncovered`/`no-audit`, reusing `isAuditFresh`/`isCoveredByParent`.
3. Wire a **non-fatal closure guard** so the non-force close/advance path warns when a root item is closed without a fresh audit and without a waiver; keep `--force` as the explicit bypass.
4. Add a read-only **`wl doctor` report** listing `completed`/`in_review` no-audit items with root/child relationship, age, and coverage/waiver status.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — New read-only `audit-gaps` subcommand (report), following the existing `foreign-items` report/`--json` pattern.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — Non-fatal warning in `closeSingle`/recursive/standard paths; honour derived child coverage and waivers.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` (or new `src/commands/audit-waive.ts`) — `wl audit-waive` / `wl audit-unwaive` commands.
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — Waiver record read/write (and nullable column in the `workitems` CREATE TABLE for new DBs).
- `src/migrations/index.ts` — Migration adding the nullable waiver column (review-gated via `wl doctor upgrade`).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — Extend the shared coverage helpers with the `covered`/`waived`/`uncovered` classification reused by CLI and herdr.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` / `src/commands/show.ts` — Surface the waiver in `wl show --json`.
- `tests/` — New tests for the guard, the report, coverage/waiver suppression, and the migration.

## Design decisions & assumptions

> These are agent-adopted decisions, recorded per the global "reasonable assumptions must be documented" rule. They are low-risk implementation choices within a clear requirement and are surfaced for producer review; a producer may override at review/plan time.

- **Flag, not hard block (AC2).** The title ("flag + doctor report"), AC1's "flags or blocks", and WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L's explicit assignment of "durable uncovered-child reporting" to this item indicate a reporting/warning guard, not a hard gate. Hard-blocking close/advance would break existing automation and force `--force` for every legacy item, so the guard warns and the report enumerates.
- **Waiver storage = nullable record, not a comment marker.** A durable, machine-readable record (persisted and surfaced in `wl show --json`) is preferred over a parsed comment, because audit comments are deprecated/non-canonical and a waiver must be queryable by the report and syncable. This is the only schema change in scope.
- **Report scope = no-audit items (AC4), coverage-aware.** The report enumerates items with **no audit record** (the accumulation problem from the description). It distinguishes covered (header/child under fresh-audited parent), waived, and genuinely uncovered. Stale-but-present audits are handled by the guard (AC2) and by the existing freshness/icon surfaces, not duplicated here.
- **Command naming.** `wl doctor audit-gaps` and `wl audit-waive`/`wl audit-unwaive` are recommended names; a reviewer/planner may rename without changing intent.
- **`--force` as waiver.** `wl close --force` already exists as the documented bypass of audit/stage checks; it is treated as an explicit waiver and (recommended) records a waiver/reason so the bypass is auditable.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Scope creep into P6 display work.** Mitigation: this item changes only the report/guard and the derived classification helper; it must not alter icon rendering or relax root-only dispatch (WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC).
- **Waiver mechanism adds a migration.** Mitigation: it is the only schema change; it is nullable, review-gated via `src/migrations/`, and old rows default to "no waiver" (fail-safe: absence never suppresses a flag).
- **False "covered" suppression.** Mitigation: coverage is depth-1 only and requires a *fresh* direct-parent audit via the shared `isAuditFresh` predicate; a missing/stale parent audit leaves the child flagged.
- **Noise in the report for legacy items.** Mitigation: the report is read-only (no `--apply`) and lists with age/relationship so operators can bulk-waive or audit deliberately rather than being forced to act.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit).** Additional opportunities (e.g. auto-audit dispatch, hard gating, bulk waiver) are out of scope and must be captured as linked work items, not absorbed here.
- **Assumption risk.** The flag-vs-block and waiver-storage decisions are agent-adopted; if a producer prefers a hard block or a comment-marker waiver, the ACs and Key Files change. Flagged for producer review.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE` — Unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher (completed). Source of the shared freshness predicate; `discovered-from` of this item.
- `WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L` — Explicit child-audit coverage so covered children are not re-dispatched (completed). Decided coverage is **derived at read time, not persisted**, and explicitly assigned **durable uncovered-child reporting** to this item.
- `WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K` — Audit freshness: content-fingerprint gate as primary (completed). The `isAuditFresh` fingerprint gate the guard must reuse.
- `WL-0MSTLFW14000KPEC` — Exclude child items from audit-tier dispatch selection (completed). Root-only dispatch; uncovered children are flagged, never dispatched.
- `WL-0MUKE17XS0030LIC` — Document derived child-audit coverage in the global audit skill (open, low). Documentation follow-on, not a blocker.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking clarifying questions were required — the seed context (including WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L's explicit assignment of uncovered-child reporting to this item and its derived-coverage decision) was sufficient to draft the brief. The genuinely open choices were design/implementation decisions, recorded above under **Design decisions & assumptions** (flag-vs-block, waiver storage, report scope, command naming) with rationale and repo evidence.

- Q: "Should the closure guard **block** or merely **flag** an unaudited completion?" — Decision (agent, pending producer confirmation): **flag** (non-fatal warning) plus a `wl doctor` report. Evidence: item title "flag + doctor report"; AC1 "flags or blocks"; WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L comment "WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG … owns durable uncovered-child reporting". Source: `wl show WL-0MUBVH8QG0020H9L --children --json`; `src/commands/close.ts`.
- Q: "How is an explicit waiver represented?" — Decision (agent, pending producer confirmation): a durable, machine-readable waiver record surfaced via `wl show --json` (recommended `wl audit-waive`/`wl audit-unwaive`), not a parsed comment. Evidence: no waiver concept existed (`rg -ni waiver src/ packages/ docs/` → none); audit comments are deprecated/non-canonical; `src/migrations/index.ts` establishes the review-gated column precedent. Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Does the report list stale audits too, or only missing audits?" — Decision (agent, pending producer confirmation): the report is scoped to **no audit record** (AC4 wording), coverage-aware; stale-but-present audits remain with the guard/icon surfaces. Evidence: AC4 "items with no audit"; problem statement "12 of 52 … have no audit record". Source: work-item description.
